decisive_items: Revealed a circumscribed tumor contiguous with adjoining normal epidermis and delineated from underlying dermis by continuous apocrine epithelial lining
Tumor epithelium with multiple papillary projections with vascular, plasma cell–rich stroma
p63 staining positive in myoepithelial cell layers
response.rationale: The tumor is well-circumscribed with an intact myoepithelial layer (p63+), favoring a benign apocrine neoplasm. The presence of papillary projections and plasma cell-rich stroma is classic for hidradenoma papilliferum. Atypia and necrosis are focal and without dermal invasion, arguing against carcinoma.

rejected.why: Nevus sebaceus is a hamartoma with epidermal and adnexal changes, not a circumscribed apocrine tumor with papillary projections and myoepithelial lining.
Apocrine gland carcinoma would show dermal invasion and loss of myoepithelial cells; the intact p63-positive myoepithelial layer and lack of invasion are against malignancy.
